title: Migrating from Semantic Kernel and AutoGen
summary: Agent Framework collapses SK's per-service agent classes into one agent type, replaces threads with sessions, replaces plugins with plain functions and tools, and replaces AutoGen teams with graph workflows and orchestrations.
useIf: You own Semantic Kernel agents or AutoGen teams and must plan a move inside the support window.
avoidIf: The code is stable, out of scope for new features and inside SK's support window: migrate on a schedule, not in a panic.

explain.md: **From Semantic Kernel (guide dated 2026-04-01).** Namespaces move from `Microsoft.SemanticKernel` to `Microsoft.Agents.AI` plus `Microsoft.Extensions.AI`; Python moves from `semantic_kernel` to `agent_framework`. There is no `Kernel` dependency. `ChatCompletionAgent`, `OpenAIAssistantAgent` and `AzureAIAgent` become `ChatClientAgent` (.NET) or `Agent` (Python), created with `AsAIAgent(...)` or `client.as_agent(...)`. The agent creates the session (`agent.CreateSessionAsync()`, `agent.create_session()`), and there is no thread deletion API: track and delete hosted threads through the provider SDK. Plugins disappear: pass functions (optionally `@tool`) to `tools`. Existing `KernelFunction` instances still work as tools through `.as_agent_framework_tool` [[tr39]].

**From AutoGen (guide dated 2026-04-01).** `AssistantAgent` is **single-turn unless `max_tool_iterations` is raised**, while `Agent` is **multi-turn by default** and keeps calling tools until it can answer. AutoGen's `Team` and `GraphFlow` map to graph `Workflow` and the built-in orchestrations; `FunctionTool` maps to `@tool`; agent middleware and sessions replace ad hoc state. The AutoGen guide says Agent Framework "focuses on single-process composition today; distributed execution is planned". That line predates the Durable Extension, which now covers durable hosting [[tr40]] [[tr30]].

blocks.code:
# before (Semantic Kernel)
# agent = ChatCompletionAgent(service=OpenAIChatCompletion(), name='Host',
#                             plugins=[SpecialsPlugin()])

# after
from agent_framework import Agent, tool
from agent_framework.foundry import FoundryChatClient

@tool(name='specials', description='List daily specials')
def specials() -> str:
    return 'Clam chowder, Cobb salad, Chai tea'

agent = Agent(client=FoundryChatClient(credential=cred), name='Host',
              instructions='Answer menu questions accurately.', tools=[specials])
session = agent.create_session()
result = await agent.run('What is on special?', session=session)

# AutoGen note: Agent keeps calling tools until it can answer
# (AssistantAgent needed max_tool_iterations > 1)

whereToUse: Planning a migration backlog for SK agents with plugins, filters and threads
Replacing AutoGen group chats with orchestrations or graph workflows
Reviewing old blog code: spotting renames such as `ChatAgent` to `Agent` and `ai_function` to `tool`
Estimating effort: which agents are simple conversions and which need redesign (distributed runtime, custom team types)

use: New work: start on Agent Framework
Old agents that need workflows, durable hosting, approvals or the Harness
Before SK support ends (at least one year after 2026-04-03, so about 2027-04 or later)
avoid: Big-bang rewrites of stable agents with no new requirements
Migrating without a regression set: defaults differ (multi-turn tool use, history storage)
Assuming AutoGen distributed runtime features map one to one
flips: A new feature needs checkpointed workflows or approvals: migrate that agent first
SK support terms change or a vulnerability goes unpatched: compress the schedule

pitfalls.symptom: An AutoGen agent that stopped after one tool call keeps looping after migration
pitfalls.cause: `Agent` is multi-turn by default, while `AssistantAgent` was single-turn
pitfalls.fix: Set explicit tool iteration and call limits on the client and add loop guards

pitfalls.cause: `Agent` is stateless between runs; history lives in the session you must pass
pitfalls.fix: Create a session and pass it on every run, then persist it

pitfalls.symptom: Imports fail on tutorials from early 2026
pitfalls.cause: Python renames: `ChatAgent` to `Agent`, `ChatMessage` to `Message`, `create_agent` to `as_agent`, `AIFunction` and `@ai_function` to `FunctionTool` and `@tool`, `SharedState` to `State`
pitfalls.fix: Follow the significant-changes page and use Learn pages with current names [[tr49]]

scenarios.title: Fifty SK agents, ten of them critical
scenarios.situation: A company has 50 SK agents. Ten are customer facing and tested well. Forty are internal helpers. The roadmap adds approval-gated workflows to three of the critical ones next quarter.
constraints: Support window until about 2027-04 at the earliest
Limited test coverage on internal helpers
unknowns: How many custom filters and plugins?
Is there an eval set per agent?
scenarios.question: How do you sequence the migration?

options.name: Migrate the three agents that need workflows first with regression evals, then critical ones, then helpers as they are touched
options.why: Value-driven order, risk contained, and evals catch default changes such as multi-turn tool use.
options.tradeoff: Two stacks run for several quarters.

options.name: Migrate all 50 in one release
options.why: Large blast radius, and the forty helpers have little test coverage.
options.tradeoff: Reasonable only with strong automated tests and a short freeze.

options.name: Wait until SK support ends
options.tradeoff: Migration becomes urgent and mistakes cost more.

flips.then: Compress the schedule and automate conversions.

scenarios.takeaway: Migrate where new capability pays first and let evals guard defaults.

scenarios.title: AutoGen group chat in production
scenarios.situation: A team runs an AutoGen `RoundRobinGroupChat` with a termination condition, plus some code on the distributed runtime. They plan to move to Agent Framework.
unknowns: How is the distributed runtime used?
scenarios.question: What is the target design?

options.name: Group chat orchestration for the chat, Durable Extension (or own checkpointed hosts) for durable execution, evals to compare behaviour
options.why: The orchestration maps directly, and durable hosting covers the distributed gap the guide mentions (checked 2026-10-13), with Beta or preview caveats.
options.tradeoff: Durable packages are Beta and preview, and behaviour differences need testing.

options.name: Port line by line to a custom workflow
options.tradeoff: More work than the built-in orchestration needs.

options.name: Wait for MAF to add a distributed runtime
options.why: The guide's 'distributed execution is planned' line is dated; the Durable Extension exists.
options.tradeoff: Valid only if your runtime needs go beyond what durable hosting offers.

flips.then: Use stable orchestration and own the hosting.

flips.if: The team needs low-level event routing
flips.then: Model it as a graph workflow with typed edges.

scenarios.takeaway: Map patterns first, then check what the runtime provides as of 2026-10-13.

quiz.q: Match the old concept to its Agent Framework counterpart.
quiz.explain: The agent classes collapse into one, threads become sessions, plugins become tools and teams become workflows.

quiz.q: After migrating, an agent that used one tool call per request makes several calls and costs more. What changed?
options: `Agent` is multi-turn by default, unlike AutoGen's `AssistantAgent`
quiz.explain: The guide says `AssistantAgent` is single-turn unless `max_tool_iterations` is raised, while `Agent` keeps invoking tools until it can return a final answer.

flashcards.back: Plain functions passed to `tools`, optionally decorated with `@tool` (Python) or wrapped by `AIFunctionFactory.Create` (.NET). `KernelFunction` can still be used via `.as_agent_framework_tool`.

flashcards.front: What default differs between AutoGen `AssistantAgent` and MAF `Agent`?
flashcards.back: AssistantAgent is single-turn unless `max_tool_iterations` is raised. `Agent` is multi-turn by default.

flashcards.front: How long is SK v1.x supported after MAF GA?
flashcards.back: At least one year (blog dated 2025-10-07). With GA on 2026-04-03: about 2027-04 at the earliest (derived).
